::: {#exr-02-quantitative-qualitative-or-mixed-interactive}
## Quantitative, qualitative or mixed?, interactive

Classify each study description by its approach. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "quant",
   "label": "Quantitative",
   "desc": "numbers, variables, testing"
  },
  {
   "id": "qual",
   "label": "Qualitative",
   "desc": "words, meanings, exploring"
  },
  {
   "id": "mixed",
   "label": "Mixed methods",
   "desc": "both kinds of data, integrated"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "A survey of 500 app users: which factors predict abandonment?",
   "b": "quant"
  },
  {
   "t": "Twelve interviews: how do people experience abandoning an app?",
   "b": "qual"
  },
  {
   "t": "A survey first, then interviews with a sample of those who quit",
   "b": "mixed"
  },
  {
   "t": "Six months of telemetry logs modelled to predict churn",
   "b": "quant"
  },
  {
   "t": "Three weeks in a security operations centre, then eight interviews",
   "b": "qual"
  },
  {
   "t": "A questionnaire (n = 412), then ten interviews on an unexpected result",
   "b": "mixed"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Closed-ended data and testing are quantitative; open-ended data and meaning are qualitative; a study that integrates both is mixed.",
 "ref": "sec-02-three-approaches",
 "reflabel": "Three approaches"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-02-the-research-onion-from-the-outside-in-interactive}
## The research onion, from the outside in, interactive

Click the six layers of the onion in the order in which they are read. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="order">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "steps": [
  "Philosophy",
  "Approach to theory development",
  "Methodological choice",
  "Strategy",
  "Time horizon",
  "Techniques and procedures"
 ],
 "explain": "The outer layers constrain the inner ones: an interpretivist philosophy combined with a large-scale survey needs explaining.",
 "ref": "sec-02-worldviews",
 "reflabel": "The research onion",
 "hint": "click the layers, outermost first"
}
</script>
</div>
```

::: {#exr-02-four-worldviews-interactive}
## Four worldviews, interactive

Place each example or description on Creswell's worldview it belongs to. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "post",
   "label": "Postpositivism"
  },
  {
   "id": "con",
   "label": "Constructivism"
  },
  {
   "id": "trans",
   "label": "Transformative"
  },
  {
   "id": "prag",
   "label": "Pragmatism"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "A/B test: which onboarding flow reduces app churn?",
   "b": "post"
  },
  {
   "t": "Interviews: what does \"secure enough\" mean to small-business sysadmins?",
   "b": "con"
  },
  {
   "t": "Co-designing an accessible web frontend with visually impaired users",
   "b": "trans"
  },
  {
   "t": "Mixed-methods evaluation of a password manager",
   "b": "prag"
  },
  {
   "t": "Knowledge is objective; found by measuring and testing causes",
   "b": "post"
  },
  {
   "t": "Knowledge is whatever works to solve the problem",
   "b": "prag"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Postpositivism measures and tests, constructivism reconstructs meaning, the transformative worldview aims at change, pragmatism lets the question decide.",
 "ref": "sec-02-worldviews",
 "reflabel": "Worldviews"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-02-deductive-reasoning-interactive}
## Deductive reasoning, interactive

Select the steps that belong to a deductive, theory-testing study. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="pick">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "options": [
  {
   "t": "Theory first, then a hypothesis",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "Data collection to test the hypothesis",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "Confirm or reject the hypothesis with statistics",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "Themes condensed from open interviews",
   "ok": false
  },
  {
   "t": "Patterns (codes) found in the data first",
   "ok": false
  },
  {
   "t": "A model of the phenomenon built as the outcome",
   "ok": false
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Deduction runs theory → hypothesis → data → confirm or reject; induction runs data → patterns → themes → theory.",
 "ref": "sec-02-worked-examples-and-tables",
 "reflabel": "Deductive and inductive reasoning"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::
